attributes.residual:
UNCHANGED from the inherited blocker; this record buys DIAGNOSIS, not score. Three findings the next lane should not re-derive.
(1) THE PLANE-POINTER WEBS ARE A PROVED CLASS BOUNDARY, NOT A LEVER. savedregs reports 'LIFETIME PERMUTATION: 3 live range(s) - r28->r29, r29->r30, r30->r28'. Target: r28=&(r3+64)=planeX, r29=&(r3+68)=planeY, r30=&(r3+72)=planeZ (ascending offset, ascending register). Ours: r29=&(r3+64), r30=&(r3+68), r28=&(r3+72). BOTH streams EMIT the three addi in the same order (+68 first, then +64, then +72), so this is purely an assignment question. Reordering the three source assignments to the target's register order changed the object but left all three rows bit-identical - per claim.law.MV that is a proved boundary: these three webs are in a numbering class that source assignment order cannot permute.
(2) THE CAMERA-FIELD BASE IS THE LARGEST UNEXPLAINED ROW. The target reads ALL SIX camera fields through the callee-saved copy r21 (`lfs f5,224(r21)`, `lfs f1,164(r21)`, `lfs f4,228(r21)`, `lfs f2,168(r21)`, `lfs f5,232(r21)`, `lfs f4,172(r21)`) while ours reads all six through the incoming formal r3 (`lfs f2,224(r3)` etc.) at the SAME displacements. Both streams execute `mr r21,r3` (target +0x1c, ours +0x24); the target simply stops using r3 immediately and ours keeps using it to +0x68. No probe this lane ran touched that, and it is the most concentrated remaining difference.
(3) THE 6 IMMEDIATE ROWS ARE NOT WRONG CONSTANTS. fndiff flags 6 same-opcode differing-literal rows and marks 6 of 6 PAIRING UNRELIABLE with drifts of -5 to -9 instructions; every one is a displacement into player/pt/cam that the aligned view shows present on both sides at its correct offset. They are the position shadow of the reorder and will resolve with it - do not record them as a constant defect (the tool's own warning names a lane that nearly did).
